Header.CaseTitle: Sunrise Hospitality Group Ltd v Grant Morrison & Co LLP

Counsel.Lead: Catherine Wilson KC; Elizabeth Clarke (instructed by Freshfields Bruckhaus Deringer LLP)

SummaryOfPosition.Summary: The Appellant claims damages for professional negligence arising from the Respondent's failure to identify material errors in the accounts of a target company, upon which the Appellant relied in making an acquisition that proved to be significantly overvalued.

FactsReliedOn.item: The Appellant engaged the Respondent to conduct financial due diligence on Prestige Hotels Ltd.
The Respondent provided a due diligence report in February 2021 confirming EBITDA of £4.2 million.
The Appellant purchased Prestige Hotels for £28 million in reliance on the due diligence report.
Post-acquisition investigation revealed that EBITDA had been materially overstated by £1.8 million.
The overstatement resulted from fictitious revenue entries and understated liabilities that should have been detected.

Contentions.item: The Respondent owed a duty of care in preparing the due diligence report.
A reasonably competent accountant would have detected the irregularities.
The Appellant relied on the report and suffered loss as a result of its inaccuracy.
The loss is within the scope of the Respondent's duty.

ReliefSought.item: Damages representing the difference between price paid and true value

AuthoritiesCited.Authority: Caparo Industries Plc v Dickman [1990] 2 AC 605
ADT Ltd v BDO Binder Hamlyn [1996] BCC 808
Moore Stephens (a firm) v Stone Rolls Ltd [2009] UKHL 39
